sentences.text: Simurghia was a pterosaur with an estimated wingspan of 5 meters.
The genus name Simurghia honors a flying beast from Persian mythology.
The species name robusta is Latin for "robust."
Isometric scaling suggests Simurghia weighed 560% more than its relative Alcione.
Simurghia was described in 2018 by Nicholas R. Longrich, David M. Martill, and Brian Andres.
All known Simurghia fossils were found during a three-year excavation that recovered approximately 200 pterosaur specimens.
The type specimen of Simurghia is a nearly complete humerus missing the head and ulnar crest.
Nyctosaurus lamegoi was transferred to the genus Simurghia in 2024.
Simurghia is similar in form but larger than Alcione and unlikely to represent an adult of that species.
Phylogenetic analysis places Simurghia as the sister taxon to Alcione elainus within the family Nyctosauridae.
Simurghia belongs to the clade Aponyctosauria.
Longrich and colleagues determined that Simurghia is a member of the family Nyctosauridae.
Simurghia lived in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 66 million years ago.
Simurghia fossils were found in upper Maastrichtian phosphates in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Northern Morocco.
The layer containing Simurghia dates to about one million years before the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.
The time range for Simurghia is estimated from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
The region where Simurghia lived contained a diverse marine ecosystem including sharks, bony fish, turtles, plesiosaurs, and mosasaurs.
